# Full text for sy documentation

# Source: README.md

## sy

`sy` is a modular desktop and agent environment for Fedora. The base RPM installs the command launcher and shared configuration tools; optional RPMs add power controls, AI inference, file management, monitoring, and other features.

You can install only the features you need. Each feature is packaged separately, while the repository keeps the commands, configs, systemd units, and package metadata together.

### Install from RPMs

The build and CI matrix currently targets Fedora 43, 44, and 45. Build packages locally with Podman or Docker:

```sh
make rpm FEDORA=44
```

Packages are written to `dist/rpm/f44/`. To install the base package and every built feature package on a fresh matching Fedora host:

```sh
make reinstall-rpm RPM_ARGS=--all
```

To rebuild and reinstall the package set already installed on the host, use `make reinstall-rpm`. For a desktop session, install `sy-desktop` as well; it supplies the declarative Niri and Waybar configuration and depends on the desktop shell. Applying the packaged configuration uses:

```sh
sudo dnf install ./dist/rpm/f44/sy-desktop-*.rpm
sy --root /usr/share/sy apply
```

The command above assumes the base and other desired packages are already installed. See the [package installation guide](docs/tutorials/getting-started.md) for selecting packages and verifying services. RPM filenames vary by release and build metadata; use the exact files generated in your output directory.

### Choose features

See the [RPM package reference](docs/reference/packages.md) for package
roles, dependencies, and feature requirements. Package metadata is
defined in [`packaging/sy.spec`](packaging/sy.spec).

### Try it

After installing the power feature in a graphical session:

```sh
sy power
```

Preview a power action without performing it:

```sh
sy power reboot --dry-run --json
```

For the AI plane, install `sy-system-aiplane`, then check its CLI and service:

```sh
sy aiplane --help
systemctl --user status sy-aiplane.service
```

NPU inference additionally needs compatible AMD Ryzen AI runtime packages and a prepared model. The AMD runtime and model files are not shipped in sy RPMs. See [NPU setup](docs/how-to/set-up-npu.md).

### Architecture

The `sy` command is the user-facing launcher. Feature crates build dedicated executables that implement their own commands and services. The RPM split lets users install features independently; shared configuration and IPC contracts connect features where needed. See [architecture](docs/explanation/architecture.md) for process and service boundaries.

### Documentation

- [Start here](docs/intro.md)
- [Tutorials](docs/tutorials/)
- [How-to guides](docs/how-to/)
- [CLI and configuration reference](docs/reference/)
- [Architecture explanation](docs/explanation/architecture.md)
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Security policy](SECURITY.md)

### Development

Build the workspace with Rust:

```sh
cargo build --workspace
make lint
make test
```

Build RPMs with `make rpm FEDORA=<release>`. See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and required checks.

### Maintainer

`sy` is maintained by [Dmitriy Gajewski](GOVERNANCE.md#roles). See [governance](GOVERNANCE.md) for project decision ownership.

### License

MIT. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

<!-- Start-here: product story first, then the Diátaxis map.

## Start here

`sy` is a modular desktop and agent environment for Fedora. The base
package provides a command launcher and configuration tools. Optional
packages add power controls, AI inference, knowledge search,
monitoring, file management, and desktop integration.

Each feature has its own executable and package boundary. Shared
configuration, systemd units, and IPC connect features where needed.
Install the features you want, then use `sy apply` to apply the
packaged desktop configuration. See the [RPM package reference](./reference/packages.md).

You do **not** need an AMD NPU, a DGX Spark, or an Android phone.
Those are extras. Bring-up is a plain laptop and a network.

![sy feature packages run on Fedora and expose commands to users and agents](./img/sy-stack.svg)

The longer story — a day using it, what is optional, why the rules
are strict — is [What sy is](./explanation/what-sy-is.md).

### What you can do

On every install:

- **Reproduce the desktop from git.** Colours, keybindings, units,
  and the bar come from `sy apply`, not from a folder of one-off
  edits. See [why there are no snowflakes](./explanation/no-snowflakes.md).
- **Search your own files.** Register a folder, index it, search
  from the CLI or from Claude / Cursor / Codex / Gemini. Tutorial:
  [search your local files](./tutorials/search-your-files.md).
- **Browse files in a window.** Super+E opens `sy file`. Markdown
  preview does not spawn Chrome. Tutorial:
  [browse files with sy file](./tutorials/browse-your-files.md).
- **Hand the same tools to an agent.** `sy auto` writes MCP server
  entries. The agent calls `knowledge_search` the way you call
  `sy knowledge search`. Tutorial:
  [drive sy from an agent](./tutorials/drive-sy-from-an-agent.md).
- **Ask why the laptop picked a power profile**, open a health
  popup (Super+M), run `sy doctor`.

If you have the hardware:

- **Ryzen AI NPU** — embeddings stay on the NPU so the GPU stays
  free for models you chat with.
  [Set up the NPU](./how-to/set-up-npu.md).
- **DGX Spark** — signed model serving on the LAN, OpenAI- and
  Anthropic-shaped URLs, Docker stays on the Spark and off the
  laptop. [Install the Spark agent](./how-to/install-spark.md).
- **Android phone** — tap to approve `sudo` over Bluetooth; if the
  phone is away, password or FIDO still works.
  [Unlock sudo with your phone](./tutorials/syauth-setup.md).

A *plane* is a feature area with commands and, where needed, a
long-running service. Planes can have separate RPM packages; install
only the ones you need. See [the package list](./reference/packages.md).

![You type a search; an agent calls the same plane over MCP](./img/sy-surfaces.svg)

[How the planes fit together](./explanation/architecture.md)
is the mechanical picture.

### Learn by doing

Follow these in order on a new laptop.

1. [Install sy from RPMs](./tutorials/getting-started.md)
2. [Search your local files](./tutorials/search-your-files.md)
3. [Browse files with sy file](./tutorials/browse-your-files.md)
4. [Drive sy from an agent](./tutorials/drive-sy-from-an-agent.md)
5. [Unlock sudo with your phone](./tutorials/syauth-setup.md) — skip
   without an Android phone.

### Look up a job or a flag

How-to (you already know the job):

- [Set up the NPU](./how-to/set-up-npu.md)
- [Add a knowledge source](./how-to/add-a-knowledge-source.md)
- [Wire MCP into your agents](./how-to/wire-mcp-into-agents.md)
- [Apply a theme](./how-to/apply-a-theme.md)
- [Run sy doctor](./how-to/run-doctor.md)
- [Install the Spark agent](./how-to/install-spark.md)
- [Serve a model on Spark](./how-to/serve-a-model-on-spark.md)
- [Run sy file from a shell](./how-to/run-sy-file.md)
- [Troubleshoot sy file](./how-to/troubleshoot-sy-file.md)
- [Write a sy plugin](./how-to/write-a-sy-plugin.md)
- [Troubleshoot a sy plugin](./how-to/troubleshoot-sy-plugin.md)
- [Troubleshoot syauth](./how-to/troubleshoot-syauth.md)

Reference (flags, schemas, words):

- [CLI](./reference/cli.md)
- [Configuration](./reference/config.md)

- [Glossary](./reference/glossary.md)

Why (design, not steps):

title: Install sy from RPMs

<!-- Template source: Good Docs Project tutorial template (CC-BY 4.0) — https://www.thegooddocsproject.dev/template/tutorial. Diátaxis quadrant: tutorial. -->

## Install sy from RPMs

In this tutorial, you build the sy RPMs for your Fedora release, install the base package and feature packages, and apply the packaged desktop configuration.

When you finish, the `sy` command is installed. If you selected `sy-desktop`, the packaged configuration is applied and the user services are available to start.

### Prerequisites

- A Fedora release listed in the [RPM package reference](../reference/packages.md).
- A graphical user session for the desktop configuration steps.
- Podman or Docker, Git, and `make`.
- `sudo` access to install RPM packages.
- A network connection for the container build and package dependencies.

### Step 1: Build the RPMs

Clone the repository and build for the Fedora release you use. This example uses Fedora 44; replace the value with your release.

```sh
mkdir -p ~/sources
git clone https://github.com/dmytrogajewski/sy.git ~/sources/sy
cd ~/sources/sy
make rpm FEDORA=44
```

The packages are written to `dist/rpm/f44/`. The script builds in a Fedora container and retains its download caches under `dist/rpm/`.

### Step 2: Install the base and feature packages

To install every package built for the host's Fedora release:

```sh
make reinstall-rpm RPM_ARGS=--all
```

This command selects the RPM directory based on the host release and invokes `sudo dnf install`. If you built for a different release, install on a matching Fedora host or rebuild for the host release first.

To choose packages manually, install `sy` and the feature RPMs you want from the matching `dist/rpm/f<release>/` directory. Package names and roles are listed in the [RPM package reference](../reference/packages.md).

### Step 3: Apply the desktop configuration

If you installed `sy-desktop`, apply its packaged configuration:

```sh
sy --root /usr/share/sy apply
```

The configuration package includes the Niri and Waybar setup. Optional feature bindings and applets appear when their packages are installed. Applying the configuration synchronizes the user units and refreshes the panel services.

### Step 4: Verify the installation

Check the launcher and installed package list:

```sh
sy --help
rpm -q sy
```

If you installed the desktop packages from a graphical session, check the panel services:

```sh
systemctl --user status sy-waybar.service sy-stack-bar.service
```

If you installed the power feature, open its menu with:

```sh
sy power
```

Use `sy power reboot --dry-run --json` to preview a power action without performing it.

### Next steps

- [Choose feature packages](../reference/packages.md)
- [Set up the optional NPU runtime](../how-to/set-up-npu.md)
- [Browse files](browse-your-files.md)
- [Search your files](search-your-files.md)
- [Read the architecture explanation](../explanation/architecture.md)

<!-- Template source: Good Docs Project explanation template (CC-BY 4.0) — https://www.thegooddocsproject.dev/template/explanation. Diátaxis quadrant: explanation. -->

## Architecture

This page explains how sy's separately packaged features fit together. For installation steps, see the [RPM tutorial](../tutorials/getting-started.md). For commands and options, see the [CLI reference](../reference/cli.md).

### Shared entry point, separate features

The RPM set has a small base package and optional feature packages. The base package installs `/usr/bin/sy`, the command launcher. Feature RPMs install dedicated executables under `/usr/libexec/sy/`; the launcher routes commands to the executable for an installed feature. See the [RPM package reference](../reference/packages.md) for package names and roles.

Feature packages include power controls, agent tools, authentication integration, AI inference, semantic knowledge, monitoring, a desktop shell, and a file manager. `sy-desktop` supplies the declarative desktop configuration and depends on `sy-desktop-shell`. Users can leave out unrelated features.

Separate executables make package installation modular. They do not mean every feature is an independent systemd service: each package owns the processes and user units required by that feature. The launcher gives users a consistent command surface across packages.

### Configuration and supervision

The repository keeps desktop templates and systemd unit definitions under `configs/`. The `sy-desktop` RPM installs the packaged configuration at `/usr/share/sy`. Run `sy --root /usr/share/sy apply` to apply it. When working from a checkout, `sy apply` uses that checkout instead.

The user-level `sy.target` groups sy's user services. Feature packages provide their own service units; installing a package does not imply that every service is always active. `sy apply` synchronizes packaged user units and desktop configuration. It also accounts for optional features installed on the host.

### Communication between features

The launcher dispatches a command to a feature executable. Long-running features communicate through the IPC interfaces documented for those services, commonly JSON messages over Unix sockets in the user runtime directory. The launcher itself does not turn every capability into one long-lived process.

The AI plane owns the AMD NPU device when NPU inference is enabled. CLI and knowledge clients use the AI service interface instead of opening a second NPU context. CPU execution does not require the AMD runtime. The `sy-system-aiplane-ryzenai` package provides host integration; AMD runtime packages and model files are external dependencies.

### Fedora and package support

The RPM build workflow currently targets Fedora 43, 44, and 45. That matrix describes package builds; a hardware-specific feature can have narrower runtime qualification. For example, Ryzen AI support depends on the separately installed AMD runtime and the host kernel/device setup. Read the [NPU setup guide](../how-to/set-up-npu.md) before enabling it.

### Why this structure

The shared repository keeps package metadata, feature code, configuration, and service definitions reviewable together. Separate RPMs let an installation include only the features it needs, while the common launcher and configuration workflow avoid requiring users to learn a different top-level command for each package.

The trade-off is that package boundaries and command routing must stay synchronized. RPM build checks and CI verify package construction; the feature reference pages describe user-visible behavior. When adding a feature, update its crate, package declaration, launcher routing, config or units as needed, and documentation together.

### Related pages

- [What sy is](what-sy-is.md)
- [Install sy from RPMs](../tutorials/getting-started.md)
- [Feature package list](../reference/packages.md)
- [ADR 0005: feature RPM boundaries](../adr/0005-feature-rpm-boundaries.md)
- [Configuration reference](../reference/config.md)
- [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md)


# Source: docs/explanation/what-sy-is.md

---
title: What sy is
sidebar_label: What sy is
